votes.reasoning: The serial drain is fixed. Cancellation now works: `withTaskCancellationHandler` sets `Cancellation`, BoundedProcess polls it every 25 ms and kills the child, and then `outcome.cancelled` or the pre-launch check throws CancellationError. onCancel also fires immediately if the task is already cancelled. The continuation always resumes by the deadline plus about 3 s, because the drains are waited on with the same deadline. Reversal test: `cancellation_kills_child` is RED on HEAD ('cancelled' false, pid alive) and GREEN with the fix. One part of point (2) of the evidence remains, and I have logged it as a new finding: if a grandchild inherits the pipe, the drain thread in BoundedProcess `drain` stays blocked in availableData until that grandchild closes it. The continuation and the caller are released, but the thread and its fd stay pinned. The finding itself marked this case as unconfirmed for agy.

The Cancellation token (BoundedProcess.swift:50-55) is Sendable, backed by OSAllocatedUnfairLock, and has no [String: Any] or unchecked escape. AntigravityExecutor wires it through withTaskCancellationHandler, and outcome.cancelled is mapped to CancellationError instead of being reported as a timeout, so no error value lies about what happened. Polling at 25 ms only runs when a stop condition exists (BoundedProcess.swift:104-106). Minor nit, not blocking: AntigravityExecutor.swift:103 calls options.cancellation?.cancel() through an Optional it just built itself. A local let would read more clearly.

AntigravityExecutor.swift:84-104: withTaskCancellationHandler sets BoundedProcess.Cancellation, which kills the child. That type is new public Sendable surface in Core, but it is lock-backed and not unsafe. It is used only here and is tested in BoundedProcessTests and AntigravityExecutorProcessTests.
